title: Retail Pharmacy Network Benefit Paper Claim Pricing Standard
content:
**Calculation.** The reimbursement approved on a paper claim under the Retail Pharmacy Network Benefit is worked out from the paper-claim submission awaiting its decision — its drug, date of service, days supply, the amount on the receipt (what the member paid) and the formulary tier on the receipt — together with the member's paid network claims for the same drug and the member's active Pharmacy Benefit Plan enrollment.

1. **Reimbursed days.** The reimbursed days of the paper claim are the days supply on the receipt.
2. **Network rate per day.** The network rate per day of the paper claim is the allowed amount of the member's most recent paid network claim for the same drug divided by that claim's days supply, or, when the member has no paid network claim for the drug, the amount on the receipt divided by the receipt's days supply.
3. **Allowed amount.** The allowed amount of the paper claim is the network rate per day multiplied by the reimbursed days, rounded to the cent.
4. **Day-supply multiple.** The day-supply multiple of the reimbursed days is one for 34 days or fewer and the network's 35-60 day multiple for 35 to 60 days. Above 60 days it is the network's 61-90 day multiple on a network that allows a 61-90 day retail supply, and otherwise one 30-day cost share for every 30 days or part of 30 days, so a paper claim is priced on its reimbursed days rather than rejected for its length.
5. **Deductible portion.** When the receipt's formulary tier is one the plan's deductible applies to, and the drug is not an insulin product (Lantus or insulin glargine-yfgn) on a plan that exempts insulin from the deductible, the deductible portion is the lesser of the allowed amount and the member's own deductible remaining — the plan's individual deductible less the deductible met on the member's active plan enrollment, never below zero — rounded to the cent. Otherwise, including a receipt that carries no formulary tier, it is zero. A paper claim is decided on the member's own enrollment record alone, so neither the family accumulation nor the Preventive Drug List exemption of the plan's deductible rule is applied to it.
6. **Tier cost share.** The tier cost share is the 30-day cost share the member's Pharmacy Benefit Plan sets for the receipt's formulary tier, applied to what the deductible portion leaves:
   - where that tier's basis is a copay, the tier copay multiplied by the day-supply multiple, but never more than the allowed amount less the deductible portion, rounded to the cent;
   - where it is coinsurance, the tier coinsurance rate multiplied by the allowed amount less the deductible portion, raised to the tier's per-fill coinsurance minimum and lowered to its per-fill coinsurance maximum where those figures are not zero, and never more than the allowed amount less the deductible portion, rounded to the cent.
7. **Member cost share.** The member cost share of the paper claim is its deductible portion plus its tier cost share.
8. **Reimbursement.** The reimbursement approved is the lesser of the allowed amount and the amount on the receipt, less the member cost share, never below zero, rounded to the cent.

The reimbursed days are settled first; the allowed amount and the member cost share are worked out on those days; the reimbursement is taken last. Rounding to the cent happens only where a clause says so.

## Worked figure (hypothetical inputs)

A member on the Northbridge Essential Network files a receipt for a tier 2 drug: 30 days supply, 120.00 USD paid. The member's most recent paid network claim for the drug had an allowed amount of 90.00 USD for 30 days. The plan's deductible applies to tier 2, the individual deductible is 500.00 USD with 480.00 USD met, and tier 2 is a 35.00 USD copay.

| Quantity | Working | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Reimbursed days | days supply on the receipt | 30 |
| Network rate per day | 90.00 USD divided by 30 | 3.00 USD |
| Allowed amount | 3.00 USD multiplied by 30 | 90.00 USD |
| Day-supply multiple | 30 days is 34 or fewer | one |
| Deductible portion | lesser of 90.00 USD and 20.00 USD remaining | 20.00 USD |
| Tier cost share | 35.00 USD multiplied by one, within 70.00 USD | 35.00 USD |
| Member cost share | 20.00 USD plus 35.00 USD | 55.00 USD |
| Reimbursement | lesser of 90.00 USD and 120.00 USD, less 55.00 USD | 35.00 USD |

## Day-supply multiple above 60 days (hypothetical receipts)

- A 75-day receipt on a network that does not allow a 61-90 day retail supply: 75 days is two full 30-day blocks and part of a third, so three 30-day cost shares.
- The same receipt on a network that allows a 61-90 day retail supply takes that network's 61-90 day multiple.

## Coinsurance tier (hypothetical)

Allowed amount 200.00 USD, deductible portion zero, tier coinsurance 25 percent with a per-fill minimum of 10.00 USD and maximum of 100.00 USD: 25 percent of 200.00 USD is 50.00 USD, which lies between the minimum and the maximum, so the tier cost share is 50.00 USD.
